text:
DeployBot: Canary deploy completed to eu-west-1 for service=runtime v3.4.2
IncidentBot: alert: p95/p99 latency spike detected on /v1/generate (eu-west-1) — p95 jumped from 120ms -> 2.1s, p99 3.7s. Error rate 5xx up to 6% (last 3m). Paging oncall.
Samir (oncall): ack — I'm on it. Pulling traces and recent deploy diff.
Raj P: what changed in v3.4.2? I only see a batching kernel tweak + kvcache affinity opt.
Tom (eng): yes batching kernel flag --enable-continuous-batching rolled in canary. Also kv cache probation change.
Elaine M: customer-impact check — any reports? Customer Ops: few errors in SLO dashboard, one customer support ticket for timeouts hitting our public API 2m ago.
Samir (oncall): quick sanity checks: hitting health endpoint returns 200. Will run load curl to replicate.
Samir (oncall): ```
# smoke load from eu-west-1
for i in {1..30}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://runtime.eu-west-1.redwood/v1/generate; done
```
Samir (oncall): seeing a mix of 200 and 504, median ~1.8s for responses that succeed. 504s align with gateway errors in front-proxy logs: ``504 upstream read timeout``.
Raj P: KV cache affinity change could cause hotshard overload on certain hosts during canary. If batch sizes increased simultaneously, that could spike tail latency.
Tom (eng): I'm seeing increased CPU wait on GPU hosts in the canary pool around the times. Might be longer kernel execs when batch bigger.
Samir (oncall): mitigation options: 1) revert canary (fast) 2) throttle canary traffic 3) switch routing to dedicated fallback model variant (lower perf but safer). I recommend revert to stop customer impact. Thoughts?
Elaine M: agree revert unless non-disruptive mitigation available quickly. Customer Ops recommends rollback to avoid more tickets.
Raj P: rollback ready, prep hotflip. DeployBot, can you cut the canary?
DeployBot: initiating rollback of rollout id=rl-8937. Canary traffic will be rebalanced over next 45s. Notifying infra.
IncidentBot: paging update: action=rollback_started, initiated_by=Samir, eta=45s. Keep thread updated. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
Samir (oncall): monitoring logs and SLO panels. Rolling back now.
Customer Ops: opening a customer-facing note: "We observed increased timeouts for a small subset of API requests following a canary deploy; we are rolling back and will update within 30m."
Samir (oncall): after rollback started, p95 trending down: 2.1s -> 250ms in 90s, error rate dropping to 0.6% -> 0.2%
Tom (eng): confirming: CPU wait and batch queue lengths back to baseline. KV access patterns normalized.
Raj P: root cause hypothesis: batching kernel path interaction with kvcache affinity produced occasional oversized batches that amplified GPU scheduling latencies, producing upstream gateway read timeouts at the proxy. We'll create a postdeploy test to simulate these patterns.
Elaine M: create customer impact summary for postmortem. Include timeline, number of customers affected, and mitigation steps.
Samir (oncall): handoff: I'll stay on until metrics stable for 30m then update incident channel. If someone wants to join a quick warroom, ping me.
IncidentBot: update: rollback complete. final p95=160ms, p99=320ms, error rate <0.5%. Incident status: mitigated.
Tom (eng): filing follow-up: create a canary-smoke test to ramp batch sizes and kvcache heat patterns, add a circuit-breaker to limit max batch in canary pools.
Raj P: creating a changelist to revert the batching flag and add canary guardrails. Will link PR here when ready.
Elaine M: good. Samir — please capture the timeline and attach logs for postmortem. Also sync with support on customer comms.
Samir (oncall): will do. Final check: any lingering customer escalations? Customer Ops: one ticket updated, customers notified, no immediate SLA claims.
Elaine M: thanks all. Marking this as mitigated for now — follow-ups tracked in #eng-runtime postmortem thread. :white_check_mark:
